newsitem.title: UK: Life term for youth who stabbed British headmaster.
newsitem.headline: Life term for youth who stabbed British headmaster.

text.p: A 16-year-old boy was given a life sentence on Thursday for stabbing to death a headmaster in a murder which shocked Britain and led to a clampdown on knives and an increase in school security.
A jury found Learco Chindamo guilty of killing 48-year-old Philip Lawrence in December as he defended a pupil from a gang of youths outside his school in west London.
Judge Neil Denison told Chindamo: "Philip Lawrence was a good man and an inspirational teacher. He dedicated and directed his life to providing a future for young people in his care.
"You took that life and diminished that future."

Lawrence's death shocked people across Britain. Prime Minister John Major led members of parliament in expressing their condolences and the Queen made a rare public donation to a fund set up in memory of the father of four.
A bill was rushed through parliament giving police new powers to arrest anyone carrying a knife in public and making it an offence to sell knives to anyone under 16.
An amnesty called after Lawrence's death led to almost 40,000 knives being handed over to police, and the government also announced moves to strengthen security in schools.
Radio listeners, deeply moved by the killing, voted Lawrence personality of the year just a few weeks after his death.

Chindamo had tried to blame the killing on another boy who was said in court to have left the country the day after the attack. But the jury of six men and six women unanimously found Chindamo guilty after a four-week trial.
Chindamo was also found guilty of wounding the 13-year-old boy Lawrence had been trying to protect.

The verdict came just a day after the government announced a crackdown on guns in the wake of another school killing -- the massacre of 16 children and their teacher by crazed gunman Thomas Hamilton in the Scottish town of Dunblane in March.

The government said all large calibre handguns would be banned and small calibre handguns used for target shooting would have to be kept under stringent security in gun clubs. Ministers are now under pressure to ban all handguns.
